Двое погибших в строительном обвале Дели

По меньшей мере два тела были найдены в северо-восточном Дели в понедельник утром после того, как спасатели провели ночную операцию на месте разрушенного дома.

Местные СМИ сообщили, что массивная плита строящегося дома упала на подрядчиков здания в воскресенье вечером, что побудило национальные и региональные спасательные команды прибыть на место происшествия.

Власти опознали погибшего как 60-летнего Чандерпала и его 36-летнего сына Виджая Кумара.

В столице Индии в последнее время обрушилось несколько зданий, поскольку незаконные сооружения, отсутствие технического обслуживания и невыполненные стандарты безопасности угрожают жизни людей. В сентябре рухнуло пятиэтажное здание, в котором проживали студенты-гостиницы, убив по меньшей мере семерых.

Амит Шах раскритиковал Харге за замечание «отца»

Министр внутренних дел Индии и правая рука премьер-министра Моди Амит Шах в понедельник раскритиковал президента оппозиции Малликарджуна Харге за «непристойное замечание» о покойном отце премьер-министра.

"Это не первый случай, когда партия Конгресса использует оскорбительные выражения против Моди Джи или его семьи. Иногда они швыряли оскорбления в его почитаемую мать, иногда называли его «торговцем смертью», а иногда издевались над его бедностью, называя его «чайвала». Под руководством Рахула Ганди партия Конгресса продолжает каждый день преодолевать границы непристойности, - сказал Шах.

Он утверждал, что ИНК принял личные замечания в «отчаянии и разочаровании» из-за потери политической базы.

BJP планирует общенациональный протест из-за замечания Моди

Партия премьер-министра Индии Нарендры Моди «Бхаратия Джаната» призвала к общенациональному протесту в понедельник из-за «непристойного и оскорбительного» замечания видного лидера оппозиции о Моди, вызвавшего споры.

Представители BJP и региональные лидеры заявили, что они организуют митинги протеста по всей стране, в том числе некоторые, которые планируют сжечь изображения.

Что вызвало спор?

Инцидент произошел на партийном мероприятии Индийского национального конгресса (INC) в восточном штате Бихар, где президент партии Малликарджун Харге говорил о спорном пересмотре списка избирателей.

Недавно партия активизировала свою годичную кампанию против премьер-министра Моди из-за заявлений об использовании процесса пересмотра для «кражи голосов». Недавний новостной репортаж о массовом удалении имен избирателей и нарушениях со стороны избирательного органа Индии также привел к крупным протестам во главе с оппозиционными партиями, группами политического давления и студенческими организациями.

На мероприятии INC Харге заявил, что все должностные лица, ответственные за нарушения в списках избирателей, включая Моди, будут отправлены в тюрьму.

В ответ на это один из зрителей выкрикнул: «Пока не будет восстания, Моди никуда не уйдет», — сообщает информационное агентство Press Trust of India. Харге ответил: «Моди ка баап бхи джайега».

Это переводится как «даже отец Моди отправится в тюрьму».

В то время как терминология является широко используемой фразой в Индии, лидеры BJP утверждали, что было глубоко оскорбительно ссылаться на покойного отца премьер-министра по поводу политики.

BJP обвинила INC в «дешевой политике»

"Малликарджун Харге, похоже, потерял всякое чувство приличия. «Modi ka baap bhi jayega» — это язык, ожидаемый от национального президента партии, которая утверждает, что поддерживает демократические ценности?, — написал представитель BJP в социальных сетях.

"Противостоять политике, но не превращайте уважение к покойным родителям в оружие вашей дешевой политики. Страна наблюдает за всем. 140 крор индийцы никогда не простят тех, кто оскорбляет их старших! Об этом сообщает BJP в социальных сетях. Кроре эквивалентен 10 миллионам в индийской системе нумерации.

Между тем, лидеры ИНК защищали Харге, говоря, что БДП также часто делала личные замечания, направленные против членов своей партии на митингах.

Добро пожаловать в наш репортаж

Доброе утро! и добро пожаловать в новостной блог DW.

Это репортаж Махимы Капур из студии Дели, где погода может стать прохладнее, но политические джебы и горящие изображения, вероятно, будут держать вещи нагретыми.

Последняя искра исходила от президента крупнейшей оппозиционной партии Индии. Президент Индийского национального конгресса Малликарджун Харге в ответ на выступление одного из членов аудитории сделал личное замечание о премьер-министре Нарендре Моди и его отце. Замечание вызвало политический скандал с политиками с обоих концов, которые столкнулись в социальных сетях, и партия Моди теперь планирует протест в понедельник.

Сообщается, что два человека погибли в результате строительного коллапса в столице Индии. Тела были найдены утром в понедельник после ночи поисково-спасательных операций.

Принц Лихтенштейнский Алоис находится в Индии с государственным визитом, в ходе которого обсуждается торговля и инвестиции, наука, технологии и инновации.

Будьте настроены на все это и многое другое!
articles.title: Новости Индии: Замечание об отце Моди вызывает политический скандал
articles.text: Импровизированное замечание лидера оппозиции в отношении премьер-министра Моди вызывает политический ажиотаж в Индии, и правящая партия планирует протест. Также принц Лихтенштейна находится в Мумбаи.

articles.originalTitle: No sign of progress in talks over detention of Japanese journalist in Russia
articles.originalText: Though Tokyo plans to continue pressing Moscow for a resolution, Russia has not softened its stance.
articles.originalFullText:
Two weeks have passed since Russian authorities detained a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun, with his detention likely to continue for some time.

The Japanese government has stepped up its efforts to secure his immediate release, but Moscow has shown no sign of softening its stance. Even a consular visit, generally provided under bilateral agreements, has yet to take place.

Tokyo plans to continue pressing Moscow for a resolution.
articles.fullText:
Прошло две недели с тех пор, как российские власти задержали японского журналиста, работающего на Хоккайдо Симбун, и его задержание, вероятно, продолжится в течение некоторого времени.

Японское правительство активизировало свои усилия по обеспечению его немедленного освобождения, но Москва не продемонстрировала никаких признаков смягчения своей позиции. Даже консульский визит, как правило, предусмотренный двусторонними соглашениями, еще не состоялся.

Токио планирует и дальше настаивать на принятии Москвой резолюции.
articles.title: Никаких признаков прогресса в переговорах о задержании японского журналиста в России нет
articles.text: Хотя Токио планирует продолжать настаивать на принятии Москвой резолюции, Россия не смягчила свою позицию.

articles.originalTitle: The key to Japan’s growth strategy: ‘proactive’ economic security
articles.originalText: The challenge is to turn ambition into sustainable growth by strengthening economic security and developing technologies that can compete globally.
articles.originalFullText:
In June, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi unveiled a long-term economic development plan calling for more than ¥370 trillion ($2.3 trillion) in public and private investment in 17 “strategic sectors” through 2041. The plan aims to create a “strong and prosperous investment framework” and earmarks ¥101.6 trillion for artificial intelligence and semiconductors alone, alongside investments in defense, space, shipbuilding and other strategic industries.

The challenge now is to turn that ambition into sustainable growth by strengthening economic security and developing technologies and industries that can compete globally. The 17 sectors span national defense, critical infrastructure, emerging technologies such as quantum computing and fusion, and food, health and energy security. Their breadth reflects the range of capabilities essential to Japan’s security.

The strategy encompasses “crisis-management investment,” including disaster preparedness, as well as economic security. It is also intended to drive economic growth. This dual purpose is both its strength and its challenge.
articles.fullText:
В июне премьер-министр Санаэ Такаичи обнародовал долгосрочный план экономического развития, предусматривающий более 370 триллионов иен (2,3 триллиона долларов) государственных и частных инвестиций в 17 «стратегических секторах» до 2041 года. План направлен на создание «сильной и процветающей инвестиционной базы» и предусматривает выделение 101,6 триллиона иен только на искусственный интеллект и полупроводники, наряду с инвестициями в оборонную, космическую, судостроительную и другие стратегические отрасли.

Сейчас задача состоит в том, чтобы превратить эти амбиции в устойчивый рост путем укрепления экономической безопасности и развития технологий и отраслей, которые могут конкурировать на глобальном уровне. 17 секторов охватывают национальную оборону, критическую инфраструктуру, новые технологии, такие как квантовые вычисления и синтез, а также продовольственную, медицинскую и энергетическую безопасность. Их широта отражает спектр возможностей, необходимых для безопасности Японии.

Стратегия включает в себя «инвестиции в управление кризисом», включая готовность к стихийным бедствиям, а также экономическую безопасность. Он также призван стимулировать экономический рост. Эта двойственная цель является как силой, так и вызовом.

articles.originalTitle: Hawks show what a modern baseball dynasty looks like
articles.originalText: The team may not win the Japan Series every year, but their droughts are never likely to last very long.
articles.originalFullText:
Among the constants in life, the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks winning the Japan Series falls somewhere between death and taxes.

The Hawks are Japanese baseball’s most dominant force — and no other team comes close.

Since 2011, SoftBank has won eight Japan Series titles in nine appearances. That run is reminiscent of past dynasties such as the Seibu Lions, who won eight titles in nine appearances between 1982 and 1992, or the legendary V9 Yomiuri Giants, who reeled off nine consecutive Japan Series triumphs from 1965 to 1973. The Giants also won titles just before that run in 1961 and 1963.
articles.title: Ястребы показали, как выглядит современная бейсбольная династия
articles.text: Команда может не выигрывать японскую серию каждый год, но их засухи никогда не будут длиться очень долго.
articles.fullText:
Среди постоянных в жизни, Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks, выигрывающий Японскую серию, находится где-то между смертью и налогами.

Ястребы являются самой доминирующей силой японского бейсбола, и ни одна другая команда не приближается.

С 2011 года SoftBank выиграл восемь титулов серии Japan Series в девяти матчах. Этот забег напоминает прошлые династии, такие как Сейбу Львы, которые выиграли восемь титулов в девяти матчах между 1982 и 1992 годами, или легендарный V9 Йомиури Гиганты, который отбил девять последовательных триумфов Японской серии с 1965 по 1973 год. Гиганты также выиграли титулы незадолго до этого в 1961 и 1963 годах.

articles.originalFullText:
THE ASSOCIATED PRESS

October 26, 2026 at 15:00 JST

Currency traders work at the foreign exchange dealing room of the Hana Bank headquarters in Seoul on Oct. 23. (AP Photo)

Shares were mostly lower Monday in Asia and oil prices fell after rising last week to their highest level in more than four years.

U.S. futures edged higher.

Analysts said investors were bracing for earnings reports of big companies and central bank decisions this week that could shake markets.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.1% to 62,602.86 and the Kospi in Seoul dropped 1.1% to 5,494.29.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng edged 0.2% higher to 23,137.93, while the Shanghai Composite index lost 0.4% to 3,673.83.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 shed 0.2% to 8,782.30.

The price of Brent crude, the international standard, fell 1.3% to $110.23 a barrel. U.S. benchmark crude sank 1.7% to $101.52 a barrel.

On Friday, the price for a barrel of Brent crude rose 3.1% to settle at $116.72, its highest level since June 2022. It has surged from less than $97 since early October.

Also Friday, the S&P 500 fell 0.5%, adding to its decline from a day before and logging its second-straight weekly loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.2%, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.2% after giving up a modest gain.

Several AI-related companies rallied, helping ease some of the impact from the broader market slide. Micron Technology rose 2.5%, Intel gained 1.7%, Microsoft added 0.7%, and Advanced Micro Devices closed 1.7% higher.

Stocks that have benefited from the frenzy over AI have been buffeted by waves of selling as investors fret over whether their high prices are justified. Many of those companies have been borrowing to fund investments in AI technology and high interest rates are making those loans more expensive.

Market players are closely watching corporate earnings, looking for a better sense of whether those investments are likely to pay off. Several influential AI-related companies report their latest financial results this week, including Google’s parent, Alphabet, along with Microsoft and Amazon.

“This week is less about broad conviction and more about proof. Big Tech now has to show that the spending binge still deserves the market’s faith,” Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management said in a commentary.

“Investors want proof now. They want to know whether the billions going into the compute buildout are building a durable earnings machine or just a shinier version of the same old capex furnace,” he said.

Industrial companies had some of the biggest losses. Caterpillar fell 2.4%.

American Express slumped 3.7%, one of several financial stocks that lost ground, despite reporting profits for its most recent quarter that beat analysts’ forecasts. The company did announce its first major job cuts in roughly a decade.

Treasury yields in the U.S. edged higher following sharp drops on Thursday.

Yields have been rising globally, partly over worries about governments taking on too much debt. Inflation also remains a concern and is stubbornly well above 3% in the U.S. That prompted the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at its last meeting in an effort to cool inflation.

Wall Street expects the central bank to hold rates steady at its meeting this week but is leaning heavily toward another rate hike in December.

This week also will bring several big economic updates, including the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation. The personal consumption expenditures index, or PCE, is expected to show that inflation rose at a 3.7% rate in September, sharply above the Fed’s 2% target.

The U.S. war with Iran has severely cut the world’s oil supply, driving energy prices higher and fueling a sharp jump in the cost of everything from gasoline to food and clothes.

In other dealings early Monday, the dollar slipped to 156.79 Japanese yen from 156.99 yen. The euro was unchanged at $1.1223.

articles.originalFullText:
REUTERS

October 26, 2026 at 14:59 JST

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspects a self-propelled howitzer as he oversees the test of key weapons, involving an upgraded version of a 240-mm, 24-tube multiple rocket launcher system, tactical ballistic missiles, and a 155-mm self-propelled howitzer, in North Korea on June 25 in this picture released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency. (KCNA via Reuters)

SEOUL―Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident, and after a North Korean howitzer was spotted close to the border.

The presence of the self-propelled 122-mm howitzer near the border as reported by Yonhap news agency on Sunday marks a rare visible deployment of such artillery.

“It is highly unusual (for North Korea) to expose its self-propelled artillery so conspicuously,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University in Seoul.

“By deliberately displaying it, North Korea is signaling through action, not words, that it intends to enforce its border policy through force rather than dialogue or negotiation.”

It is also warning South Korea to exercise caution about escalating border friction, with the intention to prevent an accidental clash, he added.

North Korean state media KCNA reported that in the letter sent on Sunday, the country’s UN representative said Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang’s border construction as a military incursion.

North Korea warned in the letter that violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defense measures and that South Korea would be “wholly accountable for all the ensuing consequences.”

PHOTOS ALSO SHOW NORTH KOREAN DRILLS

The letter is a response to a South Korean letter to the Security Council last week, which said a September 21 blast in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was planted by North Korean troops and constituted a violation of the Korean War Armistice Agreement.

The UN Command, which oversees the DMZ, has said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility.

A spokesperson for South Korea’s Unification Ministry said on Monday that the North Korean letter appears to repeat North Korea’s existing position and seeks to justify its so-called border line marking work.

The ministry had no separate comment on the placement of the howitzer. Seoul has proposed dialogue with North Korea to defuse border tensions.

North Korea’s letter also repeated accusations that South Korea had opened fire on North Korean personnel, calling that a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat or use of force against another state’s territorial integrity.

Seoul has said its military issues warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to send North Korean soldiers back across the line when they cross the military demarcation line (MDL), which bisects the DMZ.

North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years.

The Yonhap report cited photographs taken from an observatory in the South Korean border city of Gimpo that appeared to show the howitzer as well as North Korean troops conducting drills on the coast of Kaepung county, about 1.5 km (1 mile) from the observatory.

In 2015, there was a similar incident in which South Korean troops were injured by North Korean mines. Then, Seoul resumed anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts across the DMZ, triggering a military standoff. After North Korea expressed regret, the standoff ended with a high-level inter-Korean agreement.

Присутствие самоходной 122-мм гаубицы вблизи границы, как сообщило в воскресенье информационное агентство Yonhap, знаменует собой редкое видимое развертывание такой артиллерии.

«Для Северной Кореи крайне необычно так заметно разоблачать свою самоходную артиллерию», — сказал Лим Эуль-чул, профессор Университета Кюннам в Сеуле.

«Преднамеренно демонстрируя это, Северная Корея сигнализирует действиями, а не словами, что она намерена проводить свою пограничную политику силой, а не диалогом или переговорами», — говорится в заявлении.

Он также предупреждает Южную Корею проявлять осторожность в отношении эскалации пограничных трений с намерением предотвратить случайное столкновение.

Северокорейские государственные СМИ KCNA сообщили, что в письме, отправленном в воскресенье, представитель страны в ООН сказал, что Сеул использует инцидент с наземной миной, чтобы изобразить строительство границы Пхеньяна как военное вторжение.

Северная Корея предупредила в письме, что нарушения ее суверенитета могут спровоцировать меры самообороны и что Южная Корея будет «полностью отвечать за все последующие последствия».

Фотографии также показывают северокорейские дриллы

Письмо является ответом на письмо Южной Кореи в Совет Безопасности на прошлой неделе, в котором говорится, что взрыв 21 сентября в демилитаризованной зоне (ДМЗ) был заложен северокорейскими войсками и представляет собой нарушение Корейского соглашения о перемирии.

Командование ООН, которое контролирует ДМЗ, заявило, что северокорейская мина через линию нарушила перемирие. Пхеньян отрицает свою ответственность.

Представитель министерства объединения Южной Кореи заявил в понедельник, что письмо Северной Кореи, похоже, повторяет существующую позицию Северной Кореи и стремится оправдать свою так называемую работу по маркировке линии границы.

Отдельного комментария о размещении гаубицы министерство не имело. Сеул предложил провести диалог с Северной Кореей, чтобы разрядить напряженность на границе.

Письмо Северной Кореи также повторило обвинения в том, что Южная Корея открыла огонь по северокорейскому персоналу, назвав это нарушением Устава ООН, который запрещает угрозу или применение силы против территориальной целостности другого государства.

Сеул заявил, что его военные проблемы предупреждают передачи и стреляют предупредительные выстрелы, чтобы отправить северокорейских солдат обратно через линию, когда они пересекают военную демаркационную линию (MDL), которая разделяет DMZ.

В последние годы северокорейские войска строят тактические дороги и заборы, а также устанавливают мины вблизи MDL.

В докладе Yonhap приводятся фотографии, сделанные из обсерватории в южнокорейском пограничном городе Гимпо, на которых, как представляется, показана гаубица, а также северокорейские войска, проводящие учения на побережье округа Каепунг, примерно в 1,5 км (1 миля) от обсерватории.

В 2015 году произошел аналогичный инцидент, когда южнокорейские войска получили ранения от северокорейских мин. Затем Сеул возобновил антисеверокорейские акустические трансляции по всей ДМЗ, вызвав военное противостояние. После того, как Северная Корея выразила сожаление, противостояние закончилось межкорейским соглашением на высоком уровне.

Просматривайте занавес музыкальной индустрии у продюсеров, которые использовали социальные сети, чтобы помочь своим кумирам выйти на мировой уровень.

Серия, основанная на дипломатических документах, рассекреченных МИД Японии

Здесь собрана информация из первых рук о выживших после атомной бомбардировки «хибакуша».

Специалисты по кулинарии, повара и другие специалисты, занимающиеся пищевыми продуктами, представляют свои особые рецепты, переплетенные с их жизненными путями.

articles.originalTitle: 20th CPC Central Committee starts fifth plenary session
articles.originalText: The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) started its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Monday morning.
articles.originalFullText:
The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) started its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Monday morning.

Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a work report on behalf of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and expounded on a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on some major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance.

The draft decision summarizes the achievements and experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era in a truth-seeking manner and offers in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks concerning Party building at present and for some time to come. It also sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, according to a Political Bureau meeting in September that decided to submit the document to the plenum for review.

Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, full and rigorous Party self-governance has made significant progress, opened up a new frontier for the century-old Party in self-reform, and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country, said an earlier Political Bureau meeting in July that set the plenum's agenda.

The meeting said the Party and the people have won the historical initiative to build a strong Party and country but noted that as profound changes unfold in the world, in China and within the Party, efforts to exercise full and rigorous Party self-governance also face many new circumstances and challenges.

It called for adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to uphold and apply the valuable experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, resolve the prominent issues facing Party building, and consolidate and develop the sound political environment created through Party self-supervision and self-governance.
articles.title: 20-е заседание ЦК КПК открывается пятым пленарным заседанием
articles.text: 20-й Центральный комитет Коммунистической партии Китая (КПК) начал свое пятое пленарное заседание в Пекине в понедельник утром.
articles.fullText:
20-й Центральный комитет Коммунистической партии Китая (КПК) начал свое пятое пленарное заседание в Пекине в понедельник утром.

Си Цзиньпин, генеральный секретарь ЦК КПК, от имени Политбюро ЦК КПК выступил с докладом о работе и изложил проект решения ЦК КПК по ряду важных вопросов, касающихся укрепления полного и строгого партийного самоуправления с упорством.

В проекте решения кратко излагаются достижения и опыт полного и строгого партийного самоуправления в новую эпоху в порядке поиска истины и предлагается углубленный анализ ситуации и задач, касающихся партийного строительства в настоящее время и на некоторое время вперед. В нем также излагаются стратегические планы по усилению полного и строгого партийного самоуправления с упорством, согласно сентябрьскому заседанию Политбюро, на котором было принято решение представить документ на пленум для рассмотрения.

Со времени 18-го съезда КПК в 2012 году полное и строгое партийное самоуправление достигло значительного прогресса, открыло новый рубеж для вековой партии в самореформе и привело к историческим достижениям и преобразованиям в деле партии и страны, говорится на заседании Политбюро в июле, которое определило повестку дня пленума.

В ходе встречи было отмечено, что партия и народ одержали победу в исторической инициативе по созданию сильной партии и страны, но при этом отмечается, что по мере того, как в мире, в Китае и внутри партии происходят глубокие изменения, усилия по осуществлению полного и строгого партийного самоуправления также сталкиваются со многими новыми обстоятельствами и вызовами.

Она призвала к принятию более высоких стандартов и принятию более конкретных мер для поддержания и применения ценного опыта полного и строгого партийного самоуправления в новую эпоху, решения важных вопросов, стоящих перед партийным строительством, а также консолидации и развития здоровой политической среды, созданной благодаря партийному самоконтролю и самоуправлению.

articles.originalTitle: Sapporo mayoral race takes shape with Olympics and foreign population in focus
articles.originalText: Those issues, along with tourism, could prove crucial in the race to succeed Katsuhiro Akimoto.
articles.originalFullText:
SAPPORO – Sapporo’s mayoral race is taking shape after Katsuhiro Akimoto announced he will not seek a fourth term next spring.

The city’s next leader will face questions that include whether to revive Sapporo’s Olympic ambitions and how to respond to a foreign population that has nearly tripled since Akimoto’s first term.

Akimoto, who was first elected in 2015 on pledges to expand the city’s economy through tourism, said he decided not to seek another term partly because he felt he had accomplished what he set out to do.
articles.fullText:
САППОРО – Раса мэров Саппоро формируется после того, как Кацухиро Акимото объявил, что не будет добиваться четвертого срока следующей весной.

Следующий лидер города столкнется с вопросами, в том числе о том, стоит ли возрождать олимпийские амбиции Саппоро и как реагировать на иностранное население, которое почти утроилось с первого срока Акимото.

Акимото, который был впервые избран в 2015 году по обещаниям расширить экономику города с помощью туризма, сказал, что решил не искать другого срока отчасти потому, что он чувствовал, что достиг того, что намеревался сделать.
articles.title: Соревнование мэров Саппоро складывается с Олимпиадой и иностранным населением
articles.text: Эти проблемы, наряду с туризмом, могут оказаться решающими в гонке за успех Кацухиро Акимото.

articles.originalTitle: Brazil’s Lula wins record fourth term in a shock comeback
articles.originalText: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's victory was eked out in the 11th-hour after voters from his heartland rallied to the rescue.
articles.originalFullText:
Sao Paulo – Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday, the country’s electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of rightwing election victories across Latin America.

Lula, an icon of the global left and the most dominant force in Brazilian politics this century, defeated Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The senator had finished first in the election’s first round and hoped to revive his father’s far-right movement.

At times, Lula’s reelection looked like a long shot, as voters soured on him and his Workers’ Party after years of corruption scandals and rising prices, while sweeping societal changes left the former metalworker and union leader looking out of touch with an increasingly app-based economy and its growing ranks of informal workers.
articles.fullText:
Президент Бразилии Луис Инасиу Лула да Силва выиграл беспрецедентный четвертый срок в воскресенье, заявил избирательный суд страны, в результате шока, который бросил вызов опросам, прецедентам и глобальным анти-действующим настроениям, чтобы затормозить волну побед правых на выборах по всей Латинской Америке.

Лула, икона глобальных левых и самая доминирующая сила в бразильской политике в этом столетии, победил сенатора Флавио Болсонару, старшего сына бывшего президента Жаира Болсонару. Сенатор занял первое место в первом туре выборов и надеялся возродить ультраправое движение своего отца.

Время от времени переизбрание Лулы выглядело как большой шанс, поскольку избиратели испортили его и его Рабочую партию после многих лет коррупционных скандалов и роста цен, в то время как радикальные социальные изменения оставили бывшего металлиста и профсоюзного лидера вне связи со все более основанной на приложениях экономикой и ее растущими рядами неформальных работников.
articles.title: Лула выиграл рекордный четвертый срок в шоковом возвращении
articles.text: Победа президента Бразилии Луиса Инасио Лулы да Силвы была объявлена в 11-й час после того, как избиратели из его центра собрались на спасение.

articles.originalTitle: BNP Paribas AM builds long-end JGB bet on steep yield curve
articles.originalText: The bullish stance comes after superlong JGB yields reached multidecade highs this year amid concerns over inflation and fiscal spending.
articles.originalFullText:
BNP Paribas Asset Management has been raising its positions in long-dated Japanese government bonds, attracted by a steep yield curve and signs that domestic demand is returning to the market.

The firm has increased its long-end JGB position from a “very small size” early this year to a “moderate to medium size,” favoring 20- and 30-year bonds, said James McAlevey, head of global aggregate and absolute return.

“What we prefer is the long end of the market because the curve is so steep,” McAlevey said at a briefing in Tokyo last week. The sector has “significantly outperformed other global long ends” recently, providing a source of diversification, he said.

In some flexible strategies, the firm is short two- and five-year JGBs against long positions in 20- and 30-year debt, effectively betting on a flatter yield curve.

The bullish stance comes after superlong JGB yields reached multidecade highs this year amid concerns over inflation, fiscal spending and the Bank of Japan’s policy path. Elevated yields have increasingly attracted buyers, with a recent 20-year government bond auction drawing record demand.

Long-dated JGBs offer yields of around 6%-6.5% when hedged into dollars, making them particularly attractive to overseas buyers, according to McAlevey.

Domestic investors, by contrast, have been “relatively absent” from the long end as insurers grappled with impairment issues on low-coupon bonds, he said. But the strength of recent auctions suggests domestic demand is “reemerging into the long end of the JGB curve.”

Japanese insurers have been net buyers of superlong JGBs for the past four months, according to Japan Securities Dealers Association data. Several life insurers have also signaled plans to maintain or increase purchases of domestic bonds in the second half of the fiscal year.

McAlevey said a “relatively constrained fiscal response” from the government would increase his confidence in adding further JGB exposure. He is also watching whether the BOJ can maintain what he sees as a roughly quarterly pace of rate hikes.

The central bank doesn’t necessarily need to raise rates at its next meeting, he said, adding that a December move and continued relatively hawkish communication would be sufficient.

A stronger yen would further support the long end by helping contain headline inflation and easing pressure on the BOJ, McAlevey said. Yen weakness had aggravated pressure on both the bond market and the central bank earlier this year, but he sees that dynamic beginning to reverse.
articles.title: BNP Paribas AM делает долгосрочную ставку на JGB на крутой кривой доходности
articles.text: Бычья позиция появилась после того, как сверхдлинная доходность JGB достигла многолетних максимумов в этом году на фоне опасений по поводу инфляции и бюджетных расходов.
articles.fullText:
BNP Paribas Asset Management поднимает свои позиции в долгосрочных японских государственных облигациях, привлеченных крутой кривой доходности и признаками того, что внутренний спрос возвращается на рынок.

Фирма увеличила свою долгосрочную позицию в JGB с «очень небольшого размера» в начале этого года до «умеренного и среднего размера», что благоприятствует 20- и 30-летним облигациям, сказал Джеймс МакАлеви, глава глобального совокупного и абсолютного дохода.

«То, что мы предпочитаем, — это длинный конец рынка, потому что кривая настолько крутая», — сказал МакАлеви на брифинге в Токио на прошлой неделе. По его словам, в последнее время сектор «значительно превзошел другие глобальные долгосрочные цели», обеспечивая источник диверсификации.

В некоторых гибких стратегиях фирма имеет короткие двух- и пятилетние JGB против длинных позиций в 20- и 30-летнем долге, фактически делая ставку на более плоскую кривую доходности.

Бычья позиция появилась после того, как сверхдлинная доходность JGB достигла многолетних максимумов в этом году на фоне опасений по поводу инфляции, бюджетных расходов и политики Банка Японии. Повышенная доходность все больше привлекает покупателей, а последние 20-летние аукционы государственных облигаций привлекают рекордный спрос.

Долгосрочные JGB предлагают доходность около 6%-6,5% при хеджировании в долларах, что делает их особенно привлекательными для зарубежных покупателей.

Внутренние инвесторы, напротив, «относительно отсутствуют» в долгосрочной перспективе, поскольку страховщики столкнулись с проблемами обесценения облигаций с низким купоном, сказал он. Но сила недавних аукционов говорит о том, что внутренний спрос «восстанавливается в длинный конец кривой JGB».

Японские страховщики были чистыми покупателями сверхдлинных JGB в течение последних четырех месяцев, согласно данным Японской ассоциации дилеров по ценным бумагам. Несколько страховщиков жизни также сообщили о планах сохранить или увеличить покупки внутренних облигаций во второй половине финансового года.

Макалеви сказал, что «относительно ограниченный фискальный ответ» со стороны правительства повысит его уверенность в добавлении дальнейшего воздействия на JGB. Он также следит за тем, сможет ли Банк Японии поддерживать то, что он считает примерно квартальным темпом повышения ставок.

Центральный банк не обязательно должен повышать ставки на своем следующем заседании, сказал он, добавив, что декабрьского шага и продолжения относительно ястребиного общения будет достаточно.

Более сильная иена еще больше поддержит долгосрочный конец, помогая сдерживать инфляцию и ослабляя давление на Банк Японии, сказал МакАлеви. Слабость иены усилила давление на рынок облигаций и центральный банк в начале этого года, но он видит, что динамика начинает меняться.

articles.originalTitle: Government workers’ parliamentary duties linked to higher medical costs: study
articles.originalText: The findings highlight the importance of appropriate health management for government workers as concerns grow over long working hours.
articles.originalFullText:
A study by Keio University and other institutions has found a correlation between the length of parliamentary committee deliberations and higher medical expenses among national government employees working in 10 ministries and agencies in Tokyo’s Kasumigaseki district.

As concerns grow over the long hours civil servants spend responding to parliamentary inquiries, the findings highlight the importance of appropriate health management for government workers. The paper was recently published in an international occupational health journal.

A research team led by Koryu Sato, a lecturer at Keio University, examined statistical data from medical claims submitted when national government employees visited healthcare providers.

The researchers used the annual deliberation hours of standing committees in both chambers of parliament related to each ministry’s policy areas as an indicator of workload.

The study covered a period from 2016 through 2023 and about 250,000 employees between the ages of 18 and 50 who worked at the headquarters of 10 government ministries and agencies.

The team analyzed 6,454 outpatient medical claims selected for a statistical survey from claims reviewed each April.

The Health, Labor and Welfare Ministry had the highest average monthly outpatient medical expenses per employee, at ¥5,125 ($33). It was followed by the Justice Ministry, at ¥5,056, and the Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Ministry, at ¥4,637.

Mental health-related medical expenses were particularly prominent at the health ministry. The Foreign Ministry had the lowest average, at ¥2,374.

The health ministry also recorded the longest cumulative committee deliberation time over the eight-year period, at 2,534 hours — more than 1,000 hours longer than the Cabinet Office, which ranked second.

The researchers found that when the number of committee deliberation hours per employee at a ministry or agency was 1% higher in a given year, outpatient medical expenses in April of the following year tended to be 0.25% higher.

Medical expenses at the Finance Ministry were relatively low. Sato noted, however, that the Budget Committee was not included in the analysis and that employees might also find it difficult to seek medical care because of their heavy workloads.

“We used committee deliberation hours as an indicator of how busy each ministry or agency was in this study, but the working hours and workloads of national government employees must be accurately assessed,” Sato said.
articles.fullText:
Исследование, проведенное Университетом Кейо и другими учреждениями, выявило корреляцию между продолжительностью обсуждений в парламентском комитете и более высокими медицинскими расходами среди национальных государственных служащих, работающих в 10 министерствах и ведомствах в токийском районе Касумигасеки.

По мере того, как растет обеспокоенность по поводу продолжительных часов, которые государственные служащие тратят на ответы на парламентские запросы, полученные результаты подчеркивают важность надлежащего управления здравоохранением для государственных служащих. Статья была недавно опубликована в международном журнале по охране труда.

Исследовательская группа во главе с Корю Сато, преподавателем Университета Кейо, изучила статистические данные из медицинских заявлений, представленных при посещении национальных государственных служащих поставщиками медицинских услуг.

В качестве показателя рабочей нагрузки исследователи использовали ежегодные часы обсуждений постоянных комитетов в обеих палатах парламента, связанных с областями политики каждого министерства.

Исследование охватывало период с 2016 по 2023 год и около 250 000 сотрудников в возрасте от 18 до 50 лет, которые работали в штаб-квартире 10 правительственных министерств и ведомств.

Команда проанализировала 6454 амбулаторных медицинских заявления, отобранных для статистического обследования по заявлениям, рассмотренным каждый апрель.

Министерство здравоохранения, труда и социального обеспечения имеет самые высокие средние ежемесячные амбулаторные медицинские расходы на одного сотрудника в размере 5 125 иен (33 доллара США). За ним последовали Министерство юстиции в размере 5 056 иен и Министерство сельского хозяйства, лесного хозяйства и рыболовства в размере 4 637 иен.

Медицинские расходы, связанные с психическим здоровьем, были особенно заметны в министерстве здравоохранения. Министерство иностранных дел имело самый низкий средний показатель - 2374 иен.

Министерство здравоохранения также зафиксировало самое продолжительное время обсуждения в комитете за восьмилетний период, которое составило 2534 часа — более 1000 часов дольше, чем кабинет министров, который занял второе место.

Исследователи обнаружили, что, когда количество часов обсуждения в комитете на одного сотрудника в министерстве или агентстве было на 1% выше в данном году, амбулаторные медицинские расходы в апреле следующего года, как правило, были на 0,25% выше.

Медицинские расходы в Министерстве финансов были относительно низкими. Однако Сато отметил, что бюджетный комитет не был включен в анализ и что сотрудникам также может быть трудно обратиться за медицинской помощью из-за их большой рабочей нагрузки.

«Мы использовали часы обсуждения в комитете в качестве индикатора того, насколько занято каждое министерство или агентство в этом исследовании, но рабочие часы и рабочая нагрузка национальных государственных служащих должны быть точно оценены», — сказал Сато.
articles.title: Парламентские обязанности государственных служащих связаны с более высокими медицинскими расходами: исследование
articles.text: Полученные данные подчеркивают важность надлежащего управления здравоохранением для государственных служащих, поскольку проблемы растут в течение длительного рабочего времени.

articles.originalTitle: U.S. military bans Chinese-made BYD cars from key air base in Okinawa
articles.originalText: The move comes amid growing concerns about smart technology in the vehicles and the threat of spying.
articles.originalFullText:
The U.S. military has restricted vehicles made by the Chinese car manufacturer BYD from its sprawling Kadena Air Base in Okinawa Prefecture over security concerns about the vehicles.

The ban, which took effect Monday, currently only affects Kadena — one of the largest U.S. Air Force installations in the region.

The U.S. Forces in Japan did not specifically explain what prompted the move, and officials with the Kadena base did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“Installation commanders are responsible for protecting their people, facilities, and assigned missions and may implement lawful, risk-informed security measures necessary to mitigate credible threats,” USFJ spokesperson Col. John Severns said.

The ban comes as the U.S. and other Western countries have been tightening their security messaging following concerns about the smart technology used by Chinese-owned car brands such as BYD, MG and Jaecoo.

In safety advice issued in late September, the Dutch government warned that vehicles’ modern technology — including GPS, microphones, cameras, entertainment systems and Bluetooth connections — could be used for spying by state actors.

Last year, the U.S. also issued a ban on the sale of some Chinese vehicles and related hardware and software if it was deemed they could be a national security risk.

Smart vehicles have raised particular security questions for governments, given the amount of information that app developers, manufacturers and companies can access. This data is valuable to external parties or state actors who could receive the data from companies or obtain it via illegal means like hacking.

In June, the Pentagon added BYD to a blacklist of 188 “Chinese military companies” banning direct procurement or contracting with the firms.

It was not clear whether the BYD ban will be extended to other U.S. bases in Japan.

The Kadena Air Base is a crucial hub for U.S. military operations in the region. The U.S. military’s Typhon midrange missile system — believed capable of firing Tomahawk cruise missiles as far as 1,600 kilometers — is currently being stored at the base after it was deployed for joint military exercises earlier this year.

The decision to “temporarily” store the weapon there, effectively putting parts of China within striking distance, has prompted outrage in Beijing.
articles.fullText:
Американские военные ограничили транспортные средства, произведенные китайским автопроизводителем BYD, с его обширной авиабазы Кадена в префектуре Окинава из-за опасений по поводу безопасности транспортных средств.

Запрет, вступивший в силу в понедельник, в настоящее время затрагивает только Кадену - одну из крупнейших установок ВВС США в регионе.

Силы США в Японии не объяснили конкретно, что вызвало этот шаг, а официальные лица с базы в Кадене не сразу ответили на запрос о комментариях.

«Командующие установкой несут ответственность за защиту своих людей, объектов и назначенных миссий и могут осуществлять законные, информированные о рисках меры безопасности, необходимые для смягчения заслуживающих доверия угроз», — сказал представитель USFJ полковник Джон Севернс.

Запрет был введен в связи с тем, что США и другие западные страны ужесточают обмен сообщениями о безопасности после опасений по поводу интеллектуальных технологий, используемых китайскими автомобильными брендами, такими как BYD, MG и Jaecoo.

В конце сентября правительство Нидерландов предупредило, что современные технологии транспортных средств, включая GPS, микрофоны, камеры, развлекательные системы и Bluetooth-соединения, могут использоваться для шпионажа государственными субъектами.

В прошлом году США также ввели запрет на продажу некоторых китайских автомобилей и соответствующего оборудования и программного обеспечения, если это будет сочтено угрозой национальной безопасности.

Умные транспортные средства поднимают особые вопросы безопасности для правительств, учитывая объем информации, к которой могут получить доступ разработчики приложений, производители и компании. Эти данные ценны для внешних сторон или государственных субъектов, которые могут получать данные от компаний или получать их незаконными способами, такими как взлом.

В июне Пентагон включил BYD в черный список из 188 «китайских военных компаний», запрещающих прямые закупки или контракты с фирмами.

Пока неясно, будет ли запрет распространяться на другие базы США в Японии.

Авиабаза Кадена является важным центром для военных операций США в регионе. Ракетный комплекс США Typhon средней дальности, который, как полагают, способен стрелять крылатыми ракетами Tomahawk на расстояние до 1600 километров, в настоящее время хранится на базе после того, как он был развернут для совместных военных учений в начале этого года.

Решение «временно» хранить там оружие, фактически помещая части Китая на расстояние удара, вызвало возмущение в Пекине.

articles.originalTitle: Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli wins in Texas to move to brink of Formula One title
articles.originalText: Antonelli now needs to score only two points in Mexico City to be sure of the title even if rival George Russell wins.
articles.originalFullText:
Austin, Texas – Kimi Antonelli delivered a dominant U.S. Grand Prix victory for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One’s youngest-ever champion with four rounds to spare in Mexico next weekend.

The 20-year-old Italian did all he could to put the championship out of reach of his rivals in Texas, but Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton and Antonelli’s Mercedes teammate George Russell did just enough to delay the inevitable by finishing fourth and eighth respectively.

Antonelli now needs to score only two points — a ninth-place finish — in Mexico City to be sure of the title even if Russell wins.
articles.fullText:
Остин, штат Техас – Кими Антонелли одержала доминирующую победу на Гран-при США для Mercedes в воскресенье, чтобы стать самым молодым чемпионом Формулы Один с четырьмя раундами в Мексике в ближайшие выходные.

20-летний итальянец сделал все возможное, чтобы вывести чемпионат из досягаемости своих соперников в Техасе, но Льюис Хэмилтон из Ferrari и товарищ по команде «Мерседес» Джордж Рассел сделали достаточно, чтобы отложить неизбежное, финишировав четвертым и восьмым соответственно.

Антонелли теперь нужно набрать только два очка — финиш девятого места — в Мехико, чтобы быть уверенным в титуле, даже если Рассел выиграет.

articles.originalTitle: Tomoka Nishiyama to become first woman to enter kishi shogi ranks
articles.originalText: The holder of four women's shogi titles said she wants to compete against strong players and "aim higher."
articles.originalFullText:
Tomoka Nishiyama will become the first woman to enter Japan’s regular professional shogi ranks, breaking a century-old ceiling in the typically male-dominated game, after announcing Monday morning that she would exercise her newly acquired eligibility.

Nishiyama, 31, who holds four women’s titles, told a news conference in Tokyo that she had decided to become a kishi after considering her options for two weeks.

“I received warm words from many people. I also realized how strongly I wanted to compete against strong players and aim higher,” she said.

31-летняя Нишияма, обладательница четырех женских титулов, рассказала на пресс-конференции в Токио, что она решила стать киши после рассмотрения ее вариантов на две недели.

articles.originalTitle: Brazilian leftist President Lula wins reelection against conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro
articles.originalText: Leftist President Lula has defeated right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro to win a historic fourth term in office. Bolsonaro has refused to concede and called for the results to be annulled. DW has the latest.
articles.originalFullText:
What you need to know

- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro

-

It was a tight runoff, with Lula winning 51.7% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.2%, official results showed.

- Brazilians voted in the final round of the presidential election

- Lula won almost 80% of the votes cast by Brazilian voters in Germany

Keep reading for the latest updates from the second round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25:

Brazil's Lula defeats conservative Flavio Bolsonaro in presidential election

Brazilian leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in a presidential runoff, electoral authorities said.

Lula overcame his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro to secure victory in the runoff. The nearly 81-year-old leader won 51.7% of the vote, compared with 48.2% for Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

The campaign was marred by scandals and mudslinging. Sunday’s vote was thrown into confusion after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours, following Lula’s claim that buses had been taken off the roads in several cities, preventing some voters from reaching polling stations.

Pollsters said higher-than-expected turnout appeared to have benefited Lula. Conservative candidates in Brazil typically lead early in the count, while left-wing candidates gain ground as votes from poorer, more populous northeastern states come in.

In regards to foreign policy in his next term, Lula will have to manage relations with Washington while maintaining his anti-imperialist stance, as the Trump administration increasingly asserts its influence across the region. Flavio Bolsonaro had campaigned on a promise of closer cooperation with Washington.

IN PICTURES: Lula supporters celebrate, while Bolsonaro's fans disappointed

Votes tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close

The electronic voting system used in the country means that a final result could be determined within a matter of hours, although that final result is expected to be tight.

Here's a DW infographic on where the results stand:

Voting extended after complaints by both sides

Brazil's Supreme Court has moved to extend voting time in the presidential election until 7 p.m. local time (2200 GMT), giving voters an additional two hours.

The decision comes amid complaints from Lula's team that public bus services had been hampered, blocking people from getting to polling stations.

At the same time, Bolsonaro's team complained of weather conditions in certain regions making it more difficult for people to get out and vote.

Lula asks for polls to stay open longer after people 'barred from voting'

President Lula has requested an extension to poll opening hours after buses were taken out of circulation in Sao Paolo, the country's largest city, which he said prevented many people from voting.

"We are asking the Supreme Court to extend the electoral process so that those who were effectively barred from voting, due to the dirty tactics of mayors, can still cast their votes," Lula said, according to AFP.

Lula said 40% of buses in the city had been prevented from going into service, a claim that matched local media reports saying 75 buses had been blocked from leaving garages.

"I've never complained about anything in any election before. Whether I won or lost, I'd just accept it and get ready for the next one. But this time, something abominable is happening," he said.

"No one should give up on voting just because some scoundrel of a business owner or some crooked, criminal mayor tried to stop the people from casting their ballots."

Results show Brazilian voters in Germany back Lula

Brazilians in Germany have voted overwhelmingly for Lula, according to figures posted by Brazilian Embassies across the country and seen by DW's Portuguese service.

The left-wing incumbent, Lula, won 79.09% of the ballots cast by the 20,923 voters across Germany. This marks an increase on the 71.9% he won in the first round.

Brazilian voters in Germany could vote at embassies in Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich.

The German capital saw the greatest support for Lula, with 88.77% of the votes going his way. Frankfurt was the city with the greatest support for Bolsonaro, but on 29.03% he still trailed his opponent by some margin.

The turnout also increased in the second round in comparison to the first round when it stood at 19,322. However, for both rounds, only around half of the 41,552 eligible voters turned out to vote. Across the world, there are some 918,900 eligible voters for Sunday's election.

IN PHOTOS: Almost 160 million called out to vote

What role is Trump playing in Brazil's election?

Although he hasn't endorsed either candidate, US President Donald Trump is close to the Bolsonaro family.

Not only did the senior Bolsonaro imitate Trump's rhetoric and policies, he also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022, leading to his imprisonment for an attempted coup, provoking comparisons with Trump's own defeat to Joe Biden in 2020.

On the other side, Lula has presented himself as a defense against US interference.

The right "wants to govern with the American flag," Lula said after casting his ballot on Sunday.

A Bolsonaro win would mark a further move in Latin America toward pro-US far-right leaders, following in the footsteps of countries such as Colombia, Chile and Peru.

Results expected within hours of polls closing

The president of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, has said he expects the winner of Sunday's vote to be announced officially between 8.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. (2330 and 0000 GMT), according to A Folha de Sao Paolo.

Brazil uses an electronic voting system meaning that ballots can be tallied quicker than in elections where paper votes are counted by hand.

However, the gap between the winner and loser is expected to be small, with the two running head-to-head in pre-election polls.

Supreme Court president urges candidates to accept result of vote

The head of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, has called for the candidates to respect the result of Sunday's vote.

"It's important to remember that all authority and power comes from the people and, thus, it is fundamental that the choices that derive from the manifestation of popular sovereignty are respected," he said as he left his local polling station, according to A Folha de Sao Paulo.

"Brazil needs peace and calm to, from tomorrow, be able to confront the major challenges in many areas that demand the presence of the state."

Some observers have posited that Flavio Bolsonaro could refuse to accept a Lula victory, like his father before him, with the potential for violence to erupt.

IN DEPTH: What the election could mean for the Amazon

Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide.

With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

Read DW's full story on the planet-sized consequences of Brazil's election.

WATCH: One community's divide over crime and policing

Rio's deadliest police raid left 122 people dead and divided a community. As voters weigh crime against police violence, Brazil's election battle is playing out in the streets of the district of Penha.

Flavio Bolsonaro urges Brazilians to vote 'rain or shine'

Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has urged voters to turn out "rain or shine" to change the country's direction, accusing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of leaving Brazilians fearful.

"Brazil will change. Brazil will win," said the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that conditions had worsened over the past four years.

The opposition candidate criticized Lula's record on security and the economy, saying voters should not persist with a "mistake."

Bolsonaro cast his ballot at a school in Rio de Janeiro's Vila Isabel neighborhood around 20 minutes after polls opened. Wearing a yellow shirt, he arrived in the rain with his wife, Fernanda, amid heavy security.

Lula accuses Bolsonaro of preferring the US flag

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva says voters are choosing between a candidate who defends Brazil's flag and one who prefers the US flag, referring to his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.

The right "wants to govern with the American flag," the leftist incumbent said after casting his ballot in Sao Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo.

Lula, who is seeking a fourth, nonconsecutive term, also said Brazilians had taken to the streets to defend their gains.

"What I saw in this runoff was not about a political party or a trade union. People took to the streets to defend their gains," he told reporters.

He also warned about political violence, citing a brick thrown at a supporter of his leftist Workers' Party (PT) in Montes Claros. "It shows what is at stake," he said.

Welcome to our coverage

Thank you for joining us today as we bring you the latest from the final round of Brazil's presidential election.

Polls opened at 8 a.m. this morning (1100 GMT) and are set to close at 5 p.m. (2000 GMT), based on time in the capital Brasilia. The first results are expected 30-60 minutes after polls close.

President Lula, 80, is hoping to turn around his defeat in the first round to Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is currently imprisoned for trying to overturn the previous election.

Flavio has said he would free his father if he wins and give him a role in his cabinet.

Brazil's Lula defeats conservative Flavio Bolsonaro in presidential election

Brazilian leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in a presidential runoff, electoral authorities said.

Lula overcame his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro to secure victory in the runoff. The nearly 81-year-old leader won 51.7% of the vote, compared with 48.2% for Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

The campaign was marred by scandals and mudslinging. Sunday’s vote was thrown into confusion after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours, following Lula’s claim that buses had been taken off the roads in several cities, preventing some voters from reaching polling stations.

Pollsters said higher-than-expected turnout appeared to have benefited Lula. Conservative candidates in Brazil typically lead early in the count, while left-wing candidates gain ground as votes from poorer, more populous northeastern states come in.

In regards to foreign policy in his next term, Lula will have to manage relations with Washington while maintaining his anti-imperialist stance, as the Trump administration increasingly asserts its influence across the region. Flavio Bolsonaro had campaigned on a promise of closer cooperation with Washington.

IN PICTURES: Lula supporters celebrate, while Bolsonaro's fans disappointed

Votes tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close

The electronic voting system used in the country means that a final result could be determined within a matter of hours, although that final result is expected to be tight.

Here's a DW infographic on where the results stand:

Voting extended after complaints by both sides

Brazil's Supreme Court has moved to extend voting time in the presidential election until 7 p.m. local time (2200 GMT), giving voters an additional two hours.

The decision comes amid complaints from Lula's team that public bus services had been hampered, blocking people from getting to polling stations.

At the same time, Bolsonaro's team complained of weather conditions in certain regions making it more difficult for people to get out and vote.

Lula asks for polls to stay open longer after people 'barred from voting'

President Lula has requested an extension to poll opening hours after buses were taken out of circulation in Sao Paolo, the country's largest city, which he said prevented many people from voting.

"We are asking the Supreme Court to extend the electoral process so that those who were effectively barred from voting, due to the dirty tactics of mayors, can still cast their votes," Lula said, according to AFP.

Lula said 40% of buses in the city had been prevented from going into service, a claim that matched local media reports saying 75 buses had been blocked from leaving garages.

"I've never complained about anything in any election before. Whether I won or lost, I'd just accept it and get ready for the next one. But this time, something abominable is happening," he said.

"No one should give up on voting just because some scoundrel of a business owner or some crooked, criminal mayor tried to stop the people from casting their ballots."

Results show Brazilian voters in Germany back Lula

Brazilians in Germany have voted overwhelmingly for Lula, according to figures posted by Brazilian Embassies across the country and seen by DW's Portuguese service.

The left-wing incumbent, Lula, won 79.09% of the ballots cast by the 20,923 voters across Germany. This marks an increase on the 71.9% he won in the first round.

Brazilian voters in Germany could vote at embassies in Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich.

The German capital saw the greatest support for Lula, with 88.77% of the votes going his way. Frankfurt was the city with the greatest support for Bolsonaro, but on 29.03% he still trailed his opponent by some margin.

The turnout also increased in the second round in comparison to the first round when it stood at 19,322. However, for both rounds, only around half of the 41,552 eligible voters turned out to vote. Across the world, there are some 918,900 eligible voters for Sunday's election.

IN PHOTOS: Almost 160 million called out to vote

What role is Trump playing in Brazil's election?

Although he hasn't endorsed either candidate, US President Donald Trump is close to the Bolsonaro family.

Not only did the senior Bolsonaro imitate Trump's rhetoric and policies, he also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022, leading to his imprisonment for an attempted coup, provoking comparisons with Trump's own defeat to Joe Biden in 2020.

On the other side, Lula has presented himself as a defense against US interference.

The right "wants to govern with the American flag," Lula said after casting his ballot on Sunday.

A Bolsonaro win would mark a further move in Latin America toward pro-US far-right leaders, following in the footsteps of countries such as Colombia, Chile and Peru.

Results expected within hours of polls closing

The president of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, has said he expects the winner of Sunday's vote to be announced officially between 8.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. (2330 and 0000 GMT), according to A Folha de Sao Paolo.

Brazil uses an electronic voting system meaning that ballots can be tallied quicker than in elections where paper votes are counted by hand.

However, the gap between the winner and loser is expected to be small, with the two running head-to-head in pre-election polls.

Supreme Court president urges candidates to accept result of vote

The head of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, has called for the candidates to respect the result of Sunday's vote.

"It's important to remember that all authority and power comes from the people and, thus, it is fundamental that the choices that derive from the manifestation of popular sovereignty are respected," he said as he left his local polling station, according to A Folha de Sao Paulo.

"Brazil needs peace and calm to, from tomorrow, be able to confront the major challenges in many areas that demand the presence of the state."

Some observers have posited that Flavio Bolsonaro could refuse to accept a Lula victory, like his father before him, with the potential for violence to erupt.

IN DEPTH: What the election could mean for the Amazon

Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide.

With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

Read DW's full story on the planet-sized consequences of Brazil's election.

WATCH: One community's divide over crime and policing

Rio's deadliest police raid left 122 people dead and divided a community. As voters weigh crime against police violence, Brazil's election battle is playing out in the streets of the district of Penha.

Flavio Bolsonaro urges Brazilians to vote 'rain or shine'

Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has urged voters to turn out "rain or shine" to change the country's direction, accusing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of leaving Brazilians fearful.

"Brazil will change. Brazil will win," said the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that conditions had worsened over the past four years.

The opposition candidate criticized Lula's record on security and the economy, saying voters should not persist with a "mistake."

Bolsonaro cast his ballot at a school in Rio de Janeiro's Vila Isabel neighborhood around 20 minutes after polls opened. Wearing a yellow shirt, he arrived in the rain with his wife, Fernanda, amid heavy security.

Lula accuses Bolsonaro of preferring the US flag

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva says voters are choosing between a candidate who defends Brazil's flag and one who prefers the US flag, referring to his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.

The right "wants to govern with the American flag," the leftist incumbent said after casting his ballot in Sao Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo.

Lula, who is seeking a fourth, nonconsecutive term, also said Brazilians had taken to the streets to defend their gains.

"What I saw in this runoff was not about a political party or a trade union. People took to the streets to defend their gains," he told reporters.

He also warned about political violence, citing a brick thrown at a supporter of his leftist Workers' Party (PT) in Montes Claros. "It shows what is at stake," he said.

Welcome to our coverage

Thank you for joining us today as we bring you the latest from the final round of Brazil's presidential election.

Polls opened at 8 a.m. this morning (1100 GMT) and are set to close at 5 p.m. (2000 GMT), based on time in the capital Brasilia. The first results are expected 30-60 minutes after polls close.

President Lula, 80, is hoping to turn around his defeat in the first round to Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is currently imprisoned for trying to overturn the previous election.

Flavio has said he would free his father if he wins and give him a role in his cabinet.

articles.originalTitle: What to know about China’s plenum as Xi seeks stronger Communist Party discipline
articles.originalFullText:
THE ASSOCIATED PRESS

October 26, 2026 at 11:53 JST

Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a speech at the National Day reception on the eve of the 77th founding anniversary of the People's Republic of China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Sept. 30. (Pool Photo via AP)

HONG KONG—China’s political leaders and elites begin a four-day meeting Monday to discuss strengthening the ruling Communist Party’s discipline, as Chinese President Xi Jinping pushes for greater loyalty and reliability from officials while deepening his yearslong campaign against corruption.

This week’s closed-door gathering, known as the fifth plenum of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, comes roughly a year before Xi is widely expected to secure his fourth five-year term as the party’s leader and personnel changes to key leadership bodies.

While Xi has consolidated his grip on power, analysts say the plenum will offer him an opportunity to further align what Chinese officials do with what Beijing wants.

“The plenum is a chance to ensure the new generations rising the ranks share Xi’s assessment of the opportunities and risks China faces,” said Ruby Osman, a senior policy adviser at London’s Tony Blair Institute for Global Change.

Here’s what to know about one of Beijing’s most significant political meetings this year.

Xi’s anti-graft drive has been a defining feature of his rule since he came to power in 2012. Purges of officials — including some viewed as his political rivals — have been carried out on a scale that led critics to argue the campaign was also used to consolidate his power.

But his focus has expanded to cracking down on underperforming cadres too. In recent years, the number of officials punished for “formalism” and “bureaucratism” — misconduct such as dereliction of duty, inaction and reckless acts that seriously hinder development — has surged.

During the plenum, the central committee will discuss a draft policy decision on advancing “full and rigorous party self-governance,” China’s official Xinhua News Agency reported. The push could make cadres more disciplined, effective and less corrupt. The proposal reflects Xi’s emphasis on the party’s “self-revolution,” a concept centered on the party reforming itself through efforts such as rooting out corruption and building ideological commitment.

Osman said Xi’s disciplinary crackdowns are now aimed more at institutional longevity.

“It’s less about purging elite rivals and more about building a disciplined system that can sustain Xi’s political priorities across leadership cycles,” she said.

Record-high disciplinary campaigns also do not necessarily mean a rebound in corruption, but rather that Xi has been steadily raising the bar for the party’s expectations of officials, she added.

Mingda Qiu, senior analyst of Eurasia Group’s China practice, said Beijing has been building its agenda for months.

“The message is clear: the anti-corruption campaign is not winding down. Officials are not only tested for loyalty, but also for compliance and action,” he said.

Xi said in a January meeting that while decisions by the party’s top leadership were smoothly implemented in general, inspections and audits found problems such as failures to comply and improper execution, according to an October article in the Qiushi Journal, a publication of the central committee.

Xi warned against “two-faced people” who might profess political loyalty while privately defying orders and doing as they please.

“During leadership transitions, we must keep our eyes sharp, elevate good cadres who are truly loyal and reliable, consistent in word and deed, and willing to take responsibility, and never allow ‘two-faced people’ or those driven by self-interest to slip through,” Xi was quoted as saying.

The number of empty seats in the conference hall this week will help observers gauge how widespread Xi’s purges have been.

Neil Thomas, senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute, and his colleagues Lobsang Tsering and Shengyu Wang noted that while Xi’s civilian purges are record-breaking, 42 out of 44 officials affiliated with the military elected as full central committee members in 2022 have also been purged or disappeared.

The central committee started its term in 2022 with more than 370 full and alternate members. Thomas and his colleagues estimated turnout this week could be less than 80%, potentially setting a record low at any plenum since the end of former leader Mao Zedong’s rule in 1976.

Attention will also be on new demands on the officials who remain.

Thomas expects tighter scrutiny of public spending and major projects, more use of technology to uncover corruption, and tougher consequences for officials who fail to deliver on Xi’s priorities.

New personnel appointments are possible, though Xi may wait until a once-in-five-years Communist Party Congress next year to anoint his picks, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London. If he does fill any openings, it will be with loyalists, he added.

The underlying theme of the fifth plenum is that it will be another opportunity for Xi to position himself for an unprecedented fourth term in office.

Xi, who removed presidential term limits in 2018, is viewed by some as the most powerful Chinese leader since Mao. He is widely expected to be confirmed as party leader for the next term in the fall of 2027.

Ahead of that, Thomas said new ideological language reinforcing Xi’s authority might emerge at this week’s meeting.

He said the plenum should prepare the ground for Xi’s fourth term and reinforce expectations of political and policy continuity.

“After Xi has purged so many of the people that he promoted at the last congress, watch for tougher scrutiny of the officials competing to join his next leadership team,” he said.
